Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0095", "row_sha256": "8c462a21d77ac5826abeb54d5f4aa17a634687dff4b71ae31ca4226f3921e6d5", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "could you help me turn all these notes into a clear email for the families who already take lessons at Harborlight Music Studio? it’s about booking the summer block, not a general ad and not an announcement that everyone has a place already. the point is to explain how they can ask for a time and what happens after that. families know us, but they may not remember the booking dates or the way we handle requests, so make the message self-contained and warm without sounding like a sales pitch. please keep it practical, because parents will probably read it on a phone and look for the deadlines and prices first.

the summer lesson period runs from June 8 through August 14, 2026. there are no regular lessons during the week of June 29 through July 3 because the studio is closed then. please state both the full period and the closure plainly so nobody assumes lessons are happening that week. the studio is at 214 Alder Street, Room 2. Lessons are individual, not paired sibling lessons. We have in-person lessons there or online lessons, and the lesson fee is the same either way. for online, the teacher sends the Zoom link after the booking is confirmed; we don’t need to put a link in the email. students can say which format they prefer on the form, but it still depends on the teacher’s availability, so don’t make it sound like either format is guaranteed.

teachers and instruments to name are Mara Chen for piano, Joel Rivera for guitar, and Priya Nair for violin. families should request the teacher and instrument their child already studies, rather than treating this as a chance to switch instruments. lesson lengths we can offer are 30 minutes at $32 per lesson, 45 minutes at $45 per lesson, and 60 minutes at $58 per lesson. there’s no registration charge. those are per-lesson prices, not the price for the whole summer, and please make that clear enough not to be mistaken. they should select one lesson length on the booking form. we aren’t promising the same length they currently have if there’s no room in the schedule, and no need to add up or estimate each family’s total since it depends on which dates they can attend.

existing families have the first chance to request summer times from May 4 through May 10. they use the summer booking form, and the form needs to be in by Sunday, May 10. in the form they should list up to three weekly time choices, in preference order, and choose the lesson format and length too. i know people are used to their regular appointment, but they still need to put their choices in the form; we’re not automatically carrying over spring times. they can send one form for each student, even if siblings are both enrolled. make sure the email says that sending the form is a request, not a confirmed booking, and a preferred time might not be available. if somebody misses the May 10 date, they can still contact us, but the priority request window will have ended.

we’ll review the requests and email each family by May 15 to tell them whether we can offer a time. once a time is offered, they have five calendar days to reply and pay a $40 deposit per student to hold that place. the deposit goes toward that student’s summer tuition. if we can’t offer any of the three times, we’ll ask whether they want to be on the waitlist instead; there’s no deposit to join it. i don’t want the message to imply that the waitlist is a guaranteed lesson or that everybody will get their first choice. if they don’t reply within five calendar days, we may offer the time to another family. please preserve the word may, because we haven’t decided on a rigid automatic cancellation process.

there is also something Ana said when a parent asked about their usual time, and it would be useful to include it as a quote because it explains the priority period. the wording was, “I can hold your usual Tuesday slot until Friday, but I can't promise it after that.” please use that sentence exactly and introduce it as something Ana, the studio manager, said. don’t make it imply that every usual Tuesday slot is being held for every family; it was one explanation of how a requested time can remain available briefly while we are sorting requests. actually maybe keep the quote after the part about requesting times so it makes sense there, but not as the first line of the email.

families with a confirmed time will receive the lesson dates and the remaining tuition amount after they accept the offered time. they can pay the remaining amount monthly, with the first monthly invoice sent before the first lesson; don’t invent a due date for that invoice. if a family knows they will miss a particular date, they should mention it in the form, but a note about an absence doesn’t automatically create a make-up lesson. we only offer make-ups when the teacher has an opening, so don’t write a broad promise that missed lessons will be replaced. keep the request and the policy distinct: they can tell us about a planned absence, and we’ll check availability rather than guarantee a replacement.

at the end there’s a separate studio recital detail that should not get tangled up with booking or tuition. the recital is Saturday, August 15, at East Hall. taking part is optional, it is not included in lesson fees, and it needs separate registration. families should RSVP by August 1 if they want their student to participate. we haven’t said what the recital fee is, so don’t add one or suggest it is free. put this in a final paragraph so it’s clear that the recital is separate from the summer lesson booking. please organize the email so the dates, steps, costs, and conditions are easy to scan, but don’t turn it into a checklist of warnings. keep all those distinctions in there and don’t make up details we haven’t supplied.", "output": "Create a warm, practical email for current students and families at Harborlight Music Studio about requesting summer lessons. This is a booking update, not an advertisement or confirmation that every student has a place. Make it self-contained and easy to scan on a phone, with clear sections for the schedule, booking steps, prices and payment, and the separate recital information. Keep requests, offers, and confirmed bookings distinct; do not add details that are not provided.

**Summer schedule and lesson options**

The summer lesson period is June 8–August 14, 2026. The studio will be closed June 29–July 3, with no regular lessons that week. In-person lessons take place at 214 Alder Street, Room 2; online lessons are also available at the same price. For online lessons, the teacher sends a Zoom link after the booking is confirmed. Format depends on teacher availability. Lessons are individual, not paired sibling lessons.

Name the teachers and instruments: Mara Chen (piano), Joel Rivera (guitar), and Priya Nair (violin). Families should request the teacher and instrument their child already studies. Available lesson lengths and per-lesson prices are 30 minutes for $32, 45 minutes for $45, and 60 minutes for $58. There is no registration charge. These are per-lesson rates, not prices for the entire summer. Families select one length on the form; do not estimate a total, since it depends on the dates they can attend. A student’s current lesson length is not guaranteed if the schedule cannot accommodate it.

**How to request a time**

Existing families have priority to request summer times from May 4 through Sunday, May 10, 2026. Each family should submit the summer booking form by May 10, listing up to three weekly time choices in preference order and selecting a lesson format and length. Spring appointments do not carry over automatically. Families may submit one form per student, including when siblings are both enrolled. Families who miss the priority deadline may still contact the studio, but the priority request window will have ended.

Make clear that submitting a form is a request, not confirmation. Preferred times and formats may not be available, and families are not guaranteed their first choice. Include this exact quote from Ana, the studio manager, in the section about requesting times: “I can hold your usual Tuesday slot until Friday, but I can't promise it after that.” Introduce it as something Ana said, without implying that every family’s usual Tuesday slot is being held.

**Offers, deposits, and absences**

The studio will review requests and email each family by May 15 to say whether a time can be offered. Once a time is offered, the family has five calendar days to reply and pay a $40 deposit per student to hold the place. The deposit is applied toward that student’s summer tuition. If none of the three requested times can be offered, the studio will ask whether the family wants to join the waitlist. There is no deposit to join it, and a waitlist place does not guarantee a lesson. If a family does not reply within five calendar days, the studio may offer the time to another family. Retain “may”; do not turn this into an automatic cancellation rule.

Families with a confirmed time will receive the lesson dates and remaining tuition amount after accepting the offered time. The remaining amount can be paid monthly. The first monthly invoice will be sent before the first lesson; no invoice due date has been provided. Families may note planned absences on the form, but an absence does not automatically create a make-up lesson. Make-ups are available only if the teacher has an opening, so describe this as something the studio will check rather than a guaranteed replacement.

End with a separate paragraph about the optional studio recital on Saturday, August 15, at East Hall. Participation is not included in lesson fees and requires separate registration. Families who want their student to participate should RSVP by August 1. No recital fee has been provided, so do not state or imply an amount."}]
